1	# Project Landing Page - notes
2	
3	A project's own page (`/f/<id>`), a redesign of `server/views/_folder.eta` (with
4	`_branch.eta`), whose model is built in `server/main.js` (`view()` in the
5	`/f/:id` handler). Home (prelude/landing-page) gathers what needs the person
6	across projects and links here; this page holds the project's whole picture.
7	
8	Pages: `/f/:project` (Project), `/f/:project/designs/new` (New design, modal),
9	`/f/:project/branches/:branch/publish` (Push a branch, modal),
10	`/f/:project/cleanup` (Clean up, modal), `/f/:project/branches/:branch/discard`
11	(Discard a branch, modal). Fragments:
12	`/f/:project/work`, `/f/:project/app`. States: typical (spark-lending), new
13	project, app being built, update clashed (with the app on the shell's branch
14	and a failed push), long names (an existing app to connect, no remote),
15	large project (a hundred features).
16	
17	## Decisions (the person asked for all eleven, 2026-10-18)
18	
19	1. **On the design system**, not ds/v1 + `prelude.css`, like Home.
20	2. **Work beside setup**: a `.split` in a `.center.wide`. Main: Needs you, In
21	   progress, Designs. Side: The app, What the agent can read. Added
22	   `.center.wide` / `--measure-wide` to the design system (46rem can't hold a
23	   split).
24	3. **New design is a modal**, opened by the header's "New design…", the page's
25	   one primary action. A refused title comes back into the fields alone
26	   (`_new-design-fields`); made, the modal closes and the page refreshes (the
27	   real app opens the new design's page).
28	4. **One primary per view**: Merge, Push, Start the app build are plain buttons.
29	5. **A branch's state as pills**: check, building / build stopped, behind main,
30	   pull request open, nothing done yet. Stories get a state pill (Built, To
31	   build, Building) and "A change". "Also changes" is a disclosure with the
32	   full list.
33	6. **Designs show progress**: pages and how many approved or built, and when

1	# Rules: Project Landing Page
2	
3	- **R-v7q.** A project's Needs you lists the same things Home does, for that project alone, newest first, and isn't shown when nothing needs the person there.
4	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
5	- **R-2hx.** A design with a branch is listed under In progress and not under Designs; once its branch is finished, it's listed under Designs again.
6	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
7	- **R-k4n.** Pushing a branch is always asked first, saying which branch goes to which remote, and nothing is pushed until the person says yes.
8	  *shown-on: /f/:project/branches/:branch/publish @ typical*
9	- **R-8dz.** The page's work and its app follow what happens elsewhere without a reload: a turn, a build, a push or a merge changes them as it happens, and they're read again every five minutes for what Prelude can't see, such as a pull request merged on the Git server.
10	- **R-wm3.** New design offers the design system and the app shell as kinds only until the project has one of each.
11	  *shown-on: /f/:project/designs/new @ new-project*
12	- **R-r6b.** A design under Designs says it's ready to build when it has approved pages not yet built, and only once the project's app exists. A design that changed since it was approved isn't ready: it says it changed, until it's approved again.
13	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
14	- **R-h2w.** Once the app is built, it can be run from the project's own folder with a command and address of its own, never the design host's, and the Run button always shows the command it runs, so clicking it is the approval.
15	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
16	- **R-p7c.** Building or connecting the app sets how it runs from here, so a newly built app can be run without setting anything; a command changed on this page applies on this computer only.
17	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
18	- **R-5tj.** The app run from here opens in the browser once it answers at its address, and stops when Prelude quits.

1	# Clean up what Prelude leaves behind
2	
3	For anyone who has worked on a project for a while and finds old branches and worktree folders piling up. Prelude tidies a branch by itself only when all its work is in main. Everything else stays: a branch with commits after its pull request merged, a branch it lost track of, one made and never used, a folder left behind, and the copies on the remote. Today the person has to find these by hand in git. Once this is built, the project page lists them in one place, with why each is there. Only the ones that are safe to remove start picked, and nothing goes until the person says so.
4	
5	## What changes
6	
7	- When Prelude has found anything it won't tidy by itself, In progress's heading has a "Clean up…" button showing how many. With nothing in progress, a line of its own says how many branches and folders there are, with the same button.
8	- Clean up opens in a dialog over the page, titled "Clean up" and the project's name. It explains that Prelude removes a branch by itself once its work is in main, and that these are what it leaves to the person.
9	- Under "On this computer", each branch or folder shows:
10	  - its name, and what it is: "Pull request merged", "In main", "Nothing done on it", "Not in Prelude's list" or "Folder only"
11	  - warnings where work would be lost: "2 commits since", "1 commit not in main", "2 files not committed"
12	  - a sentence saying why it's there, e.g. "Made for Closing day checklist 2 weeks ago, and never worked on."
13	  - for a merged pull request with commits since, which files changed since
14	  - its folder, or that it's a branch with no worktree
15	- Only those whose work is all in main, or with nothing done, start picked. The person can pick or unpick any of them.
16	- A branch the agent is working in shows "Working" and can't be picked until its turn ends.
17	- Branches on the remote are listed apart, under "On origin". A warning says others can see them, and to pick one only if n

I've built Discard and pointed every route back at the app's views. I couldn't run anything here; Prelude's render after this turn is the first real check.

**Views** (in `server/views/projects/`)
- `_branch.eta` is ported from the design. Every branch card now ends with a quiet "Discard…" button, except while the agent is working on that branch.
- `_discard.eta` is new: the question in the modal. It says what goes with the branch, and only offers deleting the copy on `origin` (not ticked to start with) for a branch Prelude pushed.
- `page` and `_work` already matched the design exactly, so they're unchanged. The styles hadn't changed either.

**Model** (`server/project.js`): each branch in progress gains four fields:
- `ahead`: commits not in main, which the app already counted.
- `uncommitted`: changed files never committed. This costs one more git call per branch each time the work reloads.
- `inMain`: whether the design is listed on main.
- `working`: whether a turn is running in the branch.

**Handlers**
- `server/branches.js` gains `discard()`. It reuses Clean up's removal: whatever runs from the worktree is stopped, then the worktree and branch are deleted, and the branch leaves In progress. Nothing is added to Merged lately.
- The `origin` copy is deleted first, and only if ticked. If that fails, nothing on this computer is touched.
- `server/main.js` answers GET and POST `…/branches/:branch/discard`. A discard posted while a turn is running is refused and shows the question again, which then says the agent is working. A discard that fails says why beside its branch.
- Discard's URL is added to the app-layout list in `layoutOfPath`.

**Prelude files**
- routes.json: every view is `@app/...`, and the two `from`s are gone.
- RULES.md: R-w8p's *proposed* line is removed.
- NOTES.md has a "Built: Discard a branch" section.

The stories were written before Discard and don't mention it. Nothing in them disagrees with the design.

**Before you approve the screens and open the PR, look at:**
- **Typical's discard modal:** it should list Loan offers' 3 commits and say the design itself goes, since it was never merged. Underwriting queue is the one whose design is already in main.
- **A clashed update (update-clashed):** the branch card now always has an actions row, so Discard shows under "Abandon the update". That's as designed, but it's a visible change from before.
- **On a real project, deleting on `origin` deletes the remote branch,** which closes its pull request if one is open. Worth trying on a throwaway branch first.
